newsitem.title: SAUDI ARABIA: Saudi commerce minister in Geneva for WTO talks.
newsitem.headline: Saudi commerce minister in Geneva for WTO talks.

text.p: Saudi Commerce Minister Osama bin Jaafar bin Ibrahim Faqih is heading a delegation to Geneva for Tuesday's third round of talks on the kingdom's application to join the 131-member World Trade Organisation (WTO).
The official Saudi media said Faqih would present and discuss rules applicable to sectors in the kingdom including "agriculture, customs and standards and specifications".

Saudi Arabia -- the world's largest oil producer and exporter -- applied in June 1993 to join the trade watchdog's predecessor, the General Agreement on Tariffs and Trade (GATT). It held two rounds of talks in May and November 1996.
Saudi Arabia is seeking WTO membership as a developing country which would give it a special transition period to bring its legislation and practices in line with WTO rules.

Faqih told a WTO working group in Geneva at the November talks that his government was making a big effort to adapt to the WTO standards and norms for intellectual property protection -- a major concern among its trading partners.
Economists say that membership would give a boost to Saudi Arabia's plans to diversify its oil-dominated economy, build an industrial base and lure foreign investment.
